messages:
maria: Heads up — onboarding Next + Edge sample failing: Edge tsc errors and then runtime throws on default import. Anyone run into SDK overloads causing `unknown` vs `any` drift in ESM/Edge builds?
aj: Which import path? we have node and edge entrypoints; bundlers pick based on package `exports`.
maria: Using `import Inference from '@redwood/inference'` in the sample. TS reports ambiguous overloads on `generate()` and picks a narrow, node-oriented signature that resolves to `any`. Then bundler pulls a node retry util and Edge runtime errors.
kevin: Two issues: (1) package exports / ESM vs CJS resolution, (2) overload ordering + moduleResolution differences (`node` vs `nodenext`) changing inference. Ensure sample package.json has `exports` mapping and `type: "module"` so bundlers prefer the edge entry.
sam: Quick repro: set tsconfig moduleResolution to `nodenext` + module `esnext` and target `ES2022`. That aligns TSC and most bundlers. But overload selection still varies.
maria: nodenext helped but still ambiguous overload: `generate(prompt: string): Promise<string>` vs generic `generate<T>(input: T): Promise<T>`. TS sometimes picks the non-generic one depending on resolution.
aj: Fix options: reorder overloads so generic is last, or add a broad fallback signature. Also audit internal `any` usage in SDK types — those leak when consumers pull node entrypoint.
kevin: Also: ensure we ship an `index.edge.mjs` and point `exports` to it. Workaround: import `@redwood/inference/edge` for now.
maria: I'll PR sample changes and docs. Draft linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/122 (draft).
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: add edge-types CI job to `samples/.github/workflows/ci.yml` (assigned to @maria).
sam: Docs note: add a snippet in Edge onboarding about importing `/edge` and tsconfig recommendation. Saves time.
kevin: I'll take the typing audit: test TS 4.9/5.0/5.1 x moduleResolution node/nodenext and reorder overloads accordingly.
maria: Thanks — closing when PRs land.
